package.name: cloudinary
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# CLOUDINARY, fully declarative.
#
# It sat on the backlog as "blocked on `encoding: form`", and that turned out to be wrong twice over. The
# nodes used the Cloudinary SDK, so the blocker was inferred from the SDK's behaviour rather than from the
# HTTP API — and the HTTP API is kinder than the SDK:
#
#   SIGNING IS OPTIONAL. The SDK signs every upload (sorted params + api_secret, SHA-1), which the
#   expression sandbox cannot do — it has sha256 and no sha1. Cloudinary's docs offer HTTP Basic Auth
#   instead, explicitly "no signature calculation required", for the Upload API as well as the Admin API.
#   So `scheme: basic`, which already existed.
#
#   THE UPLOAD BODY IS A FORM, and their own curl example uses -F, which is multipart — the capability
#   built for ElevenLabs speech-to-text a moment earlier. `encoding: form` was never needed.
#
# The lesson is the one already recorded in the backlog: judge by the WIRE FORMAT, never by the client
# library a node happened to use.

name: cloudinary
displayName: Cloudinary
description: Upload, list and read media in Cloudinary
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1754502687/gravity/icons/cloudinary_logo.png

features:
  - Upload images and video from a URL or base64
  - List and read media already in the account

allowedHosts:
  - api.cloudinary.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [basic]
  transport: [json]
  encoding: [multipart]

credentials.cloudinaryCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# FIELD NAMES ARE SNAKE_CASE, unchanged, because that is what the stored credentials use — a credential is
# read by field name, so tidying these to camelCase would leave every existing workflow authenticating
# with three undefineds.
name: cloudinaryCredential
displayName: Cloudinary
description: Cloudinary API credentials for media management

properties:
  - name: cloud_name
    displayName: Cloud Name
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Cloudinary cloud name
  - name: api_key
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Cloudinary API key
  - name: api_secret
    displayName: API Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Cloudinary API secret

shared.credential.yaml:
# BASIC AUTH, and it is the reason this package needed no new capability.
#
# The SDK these nodes used signs every upload: sorted params, appended api_secret, SHA-1 — and the sandbox
# has no sha1, so that path would have needed a signing scheme in the executor. Cloudinary's own docs
# offer a way out: "Authenticate using your API Key and API Secret via HTTP Basic Auth (no signature
# calculation required)". Both the Admin API and the Upload API accept it.
#
# So all three nodes authenticate the same way, and the executor already had `basic`.

scheme: basic
username: "{{ credentials.cloudinaryCredential.api_key }}"
password: "{{ credentials.cloudinaryCredential.api_secret }}"

files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE GET to the ADMIN API for the asset's details. Basic Auth, like the rest of the package.
#
# THE PUBLIC ID IS IN THE PATH and may contain slashes — a folder is part of the id — so it is NOT
# encoded: `encodeURIComponent` would turn `folder/name` into `folder%2Fname`, which the Admin API reads as
# a single literal id and answers 404 for. That is the opposite of the Google Sheets range, where encoding
# was required, and the difference is worth stating because both are ids in a path.

- name: resource
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return 'https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/'
      + credentials.cloudinaryCredential.cloud_name
      + '/resources/' + ((config.file || {}).resource_type || 'image')
      + '/upload/' + ((config.file || {}).public_id || '')
  credential: { $ref: credential }
  transport: json

  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error.message || 'Cloudinary asset lookup failed'"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    file:
      type: object
      title: File
      description: >-
        The asset, as emitted by Cloudinary Files — needs at least public_id. Wire it in as an expression,
        e.g. return signal.cloudinaryfiles1.files[0]
      "ui:field": template
    transformation:
      type: string
      title: Transformation
      description: >-
        Cloudinary transformation string, e.g. w_800,c_fill,q_auto. Left blank, the asset's own URLs are
        returned unchanged.
      default: ""
    format:
      type: string
      title: Format
      description: Convert on delivery, e.g. webp. Added to the transformation as f_<format>.
      default: ""

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order": [authRequired, authRole, file, transformation, format]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: file
    type: object
    description: One asset from Cloudinary Files ({ public_id, resource_type, universalId })
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: fileContent
    type: object
    description: public_id, url, secure_url, downloadUrl, format, width, height, bytes, universalId, transformation

credentials:
  - name: cloudinaryCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: CloudinaryFileContent
kind: PromiseNode

name: Cloudinary File Content
category: Media & Design
color: "#3448C5"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1754502687/gravity/icons/cloudinary_logo.png

description: Read one Cloudinary asset's details, and build a transformed delivery URL for it.

whenToUse: >-
  Take one asset from Cloudinary Files and get its full details plus a delivery URL, optionally RESIZED or
  reformatted by a transformation. Use it when you have an asset and need a specific rendition of it; use
  Cloudinary Files to find assets in the first place.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # An asset's details are stable, but the node is cheap and a stale rendition URL is confusing, so it
  # stays honest rather than clever.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Needs the three CLOUDINARY_* variables. It reads Cloudinary's own demo asset, so it does not depend on
# anything in your account — but the ACCOUNT must be able to see it, so this is the one fixture here that
# may need a public_id of yours instead.

testData:
  config:
    file:
      public_id: sample
      resource_type: image
      universalId: abc123def456
    transformation: w_200,c_fill
    format: webp
  inputs:
    file:
      public_id: sample
      resource_type: image
  expect:
    # THE TRANSFORMATION MUST BE IN THE URL, and the format appended to it rather than replacing it — that
    # comma rule is the one detail of this node that is easy to get backwards.
    fileContent: >-
      return output.fileContent.secure_url.startsWith('https://res.cloudinary.com/')
        && output.fileContent.transformation === 'w_200,c_fill,f_webp'
        && output.fileContent.secure_url.includes('w_200,c_fill,f_webp')
        && output.fileContent.format === 'webp'
        && output.fileContent.universalId === 'abc123def456'
